title: Minimalist lateral knotless single-row versus double-row repair of posterosuperior rotator cuff tears: an ambispective cohort study of MRI-based structural healing.
summary: In rotator cuff tears (torn shoulder tendons), the tendon is reattached to the bone with small anchors. We compare two established techniques: a minimalist technique with one row of anchors and a technique with two rows. We analyse data from patients operated on at the Hessing Stiftung between 2020 and 2024 and examine them at least two years after surgery with magnetic resonance imaging of the shoulder and short questionnaires. The aim is to find out whether the minimalist technique heals as well.

interventions.name: Minimalist lateral knotless single-row repair (lateral knotless anchor row without medial row), arthroscopic or mini-open.
Double-row repair (knotted medial anchor row plus lateral fixation).

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults (≥ 18 years); complete (full-thickness) posterosuperior rotator cuff tear (supraspinatus and/or infraspinatus), Patte I–II, Goutallier I–II; primary repair at Hessing Stiftung Augsburg between 01 Jan 2020 and 01 Apr 2024 with single-row or double-row technique; preoperative MRI available.
Exclusion criteria:
Revision surgery; subscapularis involvement; Patte III; Goutallier III–IV; massive tears; partial-thickness tears; missing preoperative imaging or insufficient data; for the prospective part: contraindication to MRI, no informed consent.
